chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim bin Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn bin Sa'id, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Jameel bin Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said: I heard him say:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, cursed the one who performed a sin in Medina or gave refuge to a sinner. I said: And what is that sin? He said: Murder.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّم: Peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.مُحْدِث: One who commits a new sin

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'hadath' refer to in the Prophet's curse upon Medina?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* clarifies that the term 'hadath' (newly committed sin) in the Prophet’s curse upon Medina specifically denotes murder, highlighting the sanctity of the city as a refuge. In Shia scholarly tradition, this links the physical safety of the city with the preservation of life, emphasizing that shedding blood there constitutes a unique violation of its sacred status. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the specific legal and spiritual weight of homicide within the context of Medina's holiness.
